subfamily: Stone Fence (spirit and hard cider, Oxford STONE FENCE pdf 1931), kept still and sharp: aged rum lengthened with dry, still farmhouse cider over two or three small lumps of ice (Jerry Thomas, 1862, as Imbibe! prints him, pdf 160)
glass: heavy tumbler (about 300 ml), two or three small lumps of ice
version: v1 (Tomás, round 2, 2026-10-04). Rum : cider 3:8 (45:120). Oxford's colonial 'roughly equal' runs 22.8%, OUT of the highball band; 1:2 at 50:100 sat on the edge (17.0%) and a 43% rum sent it OUT, so the cider was lengthened toward Jerry Thomas's 'fill up the glass' (Imbibe! pdf 160). No sugar: Oxford says the Stone Fence was only 'sometimes' served with sugar. The fruit goes in raw: a thin slice of the sharpest apple to hand, cut last. Never apple brandy (the Lover family's bottle).
